extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of Renaissance literature; students studying Castiglione and courtly conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Extract prescriptive criteria and standards for the ideal courtier and court lady as reflected in the index entries to Castiglione's The Book of the Courtier. Focus on normative qualities, accomplishments, conversational rules, and duties mentioned in the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentle birth requisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Birth, gentle, requisite in the courtier (index references to pp. 33-35).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original index statement: 'Birth, gentle, requisite in the courtier, 33-5.' Implies social origin (gentle birth) is listed as a formal prerequisite for the ideal courtier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace (cultivated, avoid affectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace requisite in the courtier; cannot be learned but may be cultivated; lies chiefly in the avoidance of affectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lines: 'Grace : cannot be learned, but may be cultivated, 34; lies chiefly in the avoidance of affectation, 35' and 'Grace requisite in the courtier, 33.' Guidance: stresses natural ease refined by practice and avoidance of artificial behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumspection necessary to the courtier; even more necessary to the court lady.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Circumspection : necessary to the courtier, 59; even more necessary to the court lady, 176.' Emphasizes prudent judgment and discretion in action and speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of friends
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of friends; peril of too blind confidence in friends; reciprocal duties of friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries: 'Choice of friends, 105-7' and 'Friends : choice of, 105-7; peril of too blind confidence in, 106; reciprocal duties of, 107.' Guidance includes selecting friends wisely and mutual obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct (rules for behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and propounded maxims of conduct for the courtier (e.g., Federico Fregoso's rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Conduct, Federico Fregoso propounds rules of, 83.' Implies explicit behavioral prescriptions appear in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concealment of art / openness about good deeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Concealment of art: the courtier need not conceal his good deeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Concealment: of art, 35; the courtier need not conceal his good deeds, 84.' Distinguishes between concealing technical art and not hiding virtuous acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage requisite in the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index statement: 'Courage requisite in the courtier, 35.' A personal virtue expected of the ideal courtier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costume and dress as index of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Costume appropriate to the courtier; the courtier's dress as an index of character; remarks on court lady's dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lines: 'Costume appropriate to the courtier, 103-4' and 'Dress : the courtier's, 102-4; an index of character, 103-5; the court lady's, 179-80.' Guidance: dress should reflect fitness for court and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court lady: attributes and accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: The court lady must be womanly; possess beauty; be affable, vivacious, witty, not too prudish; not too familiar nor a scandal-monger; tactful in conversation; avoid over-rugged exercises; her dress; must be well informed and accomplished in literature, music, painting and dancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index passage: 'Court Lady, the: ... must be womanly, 175; her need of beauty, 176; must be affable, vivacious, witty, not too prudish, 176; not too familiar, not a scandal-monger, tactful in conversation, 177-8; not addicted to over-rugged exercises, or too ready to dance or sing, 179; her dress, 179-80; must be no less well informed than the courtier, and understand even those exercises that she does not practise; she must also be accomplished in literature, music, painting and dancing, 180; Pallavicino objects to such multiplicity of acquirement, 181-2.' This bundles the index's standards for ideal female courtiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtiers' duty to influence prince morally
rubrics_metrics.description: Courtiers' duty to entice their prince towards virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Courtiers' duty to entice their prince towards virtue, 350-1.' Positions the courtier as an ethical guide to the ruler.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtiership: perfection and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the subject 'courtiership', its perfection, and proper aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Courtiership: the subject of the book, 7; beginning of the discussion concerning the perfection of, 19; beginning of the discussion concerning the proper aims of, 246; explanation of the word, 335.' This sets the overall evaluative frame for what makes a perfect courtier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deserve (merit as way to win favour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to win princes' favour is to deserve it — merit-based approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Deserve, the best way to win princes' favour is to deserve it, 96.' Advises earning favour through merit rather than flattery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises: appropriate vs inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: List and guidance on exercises proper for the courtier and those inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Exercises: those proper for the courtier, 39-31; those inappropriate for the courtier, 31.' Also mentions specific exercises (horsemanship, leaping, dancing, duels, etc.) elsewhere; implies a standard of suitable bodily accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment (manner/time) of accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the manner and timing of employing the courtier's accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Manner and time of employing the courtier's accomplishments, 81 et seq.' Guidance: discretion about when to display skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment of the cavalier
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessity for proper equipment for the cavalier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Equipment of the cavalier, the necessity for proper, 85.' Material preparedness as part of courtly competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favours: generally not to be sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Favours are not in general to be sought by the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Favours, not in general to be sought, 94-6.' Encourages restraint and dignity in seeking patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: First impression importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The courtier should strive to make a good first impression; illustrated with an amusing story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'First impression : amusing story illustrating the importance of, 113; the courtier to try to make a good, 123.' Emphasizes initial presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Games and pastimes appropriate for court
rubrics_metrics.description: Games proposed by various members of the court; chase, hunting, dancing, cards and dice, etc., as appropriate pastimes for courtiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries: 'Games proposed by various members of the court, 23-9'; 'Chase: an appropriate pastime for the courtier, 31'; 'Cards and dice, 108'; 'Chess: 108-9.' Guidance: recommends suitable leisure activities fitting courtly station.

rubrics_metrics.name: General repute / reputation matters
rubrics_metrics.description: General repute and its influence; the importance of social reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'General repute, illustrations of the influence of, 123.' Reputation is treated as a substantive factor in court success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and uprightness
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty and uprightness are requisite in the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Honesty and uprightness, requisite in the courtier, 56.' Stresses moral qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty is requisite in the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Loyalty requisite in the courtier, 25.' A core expected virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of envy and disparagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The courtier should avoid arousing envy; disparagement to be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Envy, the courtier to avoid arousing, 86' and 'Disparagement, to be avoided, 115-6.' Guidance: manage behaviour and praise to prevent jealousy and rudeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation: adapt to company and avoid improbabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversation should be varied to suit the company; avoid improbabilities and certain kinds of pleasantries; tact and moderation in talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Conversation, to be varied to suit the company, 93' and 'Improbabilities, to be avoided in conversation, 119.' Also references avoidance of excessive freedom of manners (114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour: sources and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of humour; incongruity as source of laughter; limits to ridiculing defects and foibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Humour, beginning of the discussion on, 130' and 'Incongruity, the source of laughter, 134' and 'Defects and foibles, limits to be observed in ridiculing, 138.' Guidance: use wit but avoid cruelty and impropriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning and letters (humanities/history/knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The courtier should be versed in the humanities, history, letters; knowledge is essential to literary style; letters are the true ornament of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries: 'Humanities, the courtier to be versed in, 59'; 'History, the courtier to be versed in, 59'; 'Letters: the true ornament of the mind, 56.' Also discussion of imitation, literary style and knowledge (38-54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages: Greek and Latin competence
rubrics_metrics.description: The courtier ought to know many languages and be conversant with Greek and Latin; preference for Greek in some notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Languages, the courtier ought to know many, 115' and 'Greek : the courtier to be conversant with, 59; Castiglione prefers that his son should devote less attention to Latin than to Greek, 347.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing and artistic accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing is a necessary accomplishment for the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Drawing, a necessary accomplishment for the courtier, 65.' Part of the recommended arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horsemanship and martial accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: The courtier must be adept in horsemanship and martial exercises; specific martial skills and equipment are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Horsemanship, the courtier to be an adept in, 30' and 'Equipment of the cavalier, the necessity for proper, 85' plus mentions of other martial exercises (30-31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dancing and leaping
rubrics_metrics.description: Dancing and leaping are listed among accomplishments proper for the courtier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Dancing : affectation in, 36; how to be practised, 56-7' and 'Leaping, an accomplishment proper for the courtier, 31.' Guidance: physical graces to be cultivated without affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love and sexual/romantic conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing love: conduct for women (married/unmarried), how men should win and declare love, openness vs secrecy, how love is retained, rivalry, whether love is seemly for old courtiers, distinctions between carnal and spiritual (Platonic/divine) love, and invocation to divine love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index gives extensive cross-references: 'Love : the course to be pursued by women (married and unmarried) in love, 223-40; how men are to win women's love, 229-30; how men are to declare their love, 231-2; openness in love, 233-4; how love is retained, 234-6; rivalry in love, 334-6; secrecy in love, 237-40; whether love be seemly in an old courtier, 286-7; Bembo's discourse on Platonic love, 288-307; love defined as "a certain desire to enjoy beauty," 288; defects of carnal love, 290; spiritual love, 304-5; Bembo's invocation to divine love, 305-7.' This bundles the work's prescriptive norms on erotic and spiritual love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation, continence and temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: Continence and temperance discussed and contrasted; continence of Scipio used as example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Continence and temperance, contrasted and discussed, 357' and 'Continence of Scipio, the story of the, 307-8.' Guidance: self-control as an admired quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public virtues and duties of princes (context for courtier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties and standards for princes that contextually affect the courtier: justice as first care, generosity, magnificence, good government forms, liberty, and law-respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries: 'Justice, the good prince's first care, 370'; 'Generosity, a duty of princes, 273-4'; 'Magnificence, a duty of princes, 273-4'; 'Good government, three forms of, 260'; and 'Law, princes' need to show respect for, 371.' While these are standards for rulers, they form part of the normative environment for the courtier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of falsehood and ignorance as princely/court faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsehood and ignorance are identified as sources of princes' errors; ignorance is root of evil; courtier should be mindful of this climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: 'Falsehood, the origin of princes' errours, 348' and 'Ignorance : as to confessing, 116-7; one of the gravest faults of princes, 247; the root of evil, 354-6.' Guidance: underscores the value of truth and knowledge in courtly life.
